stage1.impression: This reads as a real-time render of a showroom. A dead-centre, symmetric box lined in even, laminate-like planks, with a flat, featureless brown floor and a black void around it. The two speakers read as pale grey appliances with glowing white blocks, not as smoked acrylic, and a blown white disc fills the bottom of the frame where the photographer's foreground should be. A design magazine would not publish it as a specific place: it is a generic hi-fi room, with no concrete, beams, steel, life or pools of light.

blocking_9: The frame must read as a specific room: board-formed concrete, Douglas fir beams or blackened steel visible at 1:1 somewhere in the frame. Right now only an evenly lit plank box shows, inside a flat dark void.
Pools of light and falloff: the floor band [0,560,1200,700] must show lum_range >= 45 (now 17.4), and the fir wall must fall off rather than read as a uniform wash.
The foreground practical must read as a lamp, with its tinted shell, frosted liner and rim legible, not as a flat white disc (now median 216).
A seated, off-axis, lived-in viewpoint with a glass, a coat and a record in sharp mid-ground. The perfectly symmetric eye-level view reads as CG.
The speakers must read as smoked cast acrylic with light passing through it. Now the cabinet region is neutral grey (R104 G94 B94), and the white batts and pale frame dominate.
No saturated colour anywhere: in the Smoke configuration the hero speaker carries no tint, so the 'one colour from the speaker' read fails.

defects.what: Foreground lamp reads as a blown, flat white disc (median 216) with no form, liner or rim. It looks like a plate or a hole in the image.
Floor is a dead flat brown plane (lum_range 17.4), with no pools, no reflections of the speakers or plinths, and no texture.
Fir lining reads as tiled laminate: regular planks of equal width, repeated grain, no checks, nail holes or end grain. The light across it is uniform (profile 76 to 86 down the wall).
Ceiling and surround are an empty dark void (lum_range 37, no detail). No concrete, beams or structure are visible anywhere in the frame.
Speaker cabinets read as pale grey boxes: the white batts and light frame look like opaque plastic blocks, and nothing shows as tinted or smoked acrylic.
The horn's gloss shows smeared, wobbly reflections and a thin white outline, which reads as a CG specular.
Plinth top edge glows hard white and clips (clip 1.14 %). It reads as an LED strip, closer to a display case than a piece of furniture.
Sleeve against the right plinth reads as a blank cardboard box with no artwork or edge thickness.
Tub chairs are blobby, cut-off silhouettes with no velvet pile, seams or legs.
Perfect bilateral symmetry and an identical copy of the speaker and plinth on each side. With one-point perspective on a box, the frame reads as a game or configurator.
Rocks glass is dark and murky, with no rim highlight or liquid read, and it is partly hidden behind the lamp.

out_of_scope.request: Make the speaker the frame's one saturated colour (a tinted configuration instead of Smoke).
out_of_scope.why: The configuration and the products' tint are fixed. In Smoke the hero carries no saturated colour, so the 'one colour' read cannot be met in this frame.

out_of_scope.request: Make the speakers' white batts and pale inner frame read less like opaque plastic blocks.
out_of_scope.why: These are the speaker's parts (white batts inside, cover off), which are fixed.

out_of_scope.request: Break the uniform fir lining with beams, concrete or steel in view, or change the niche's plank pattern.
out_of_scope.why: The room's design and materials are fixed. A camera move (c1) that brings the side walls and ceiling structure into view is the allowed route.

out_of_scope.request: Give the tub chairs more defined form (pile, seams, legs).
out_of_scope.why: The seats are fixed by the room's design. Light and camera can only help them read.
